transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card services. My name is Sarah. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Hi, yes, this is Marcus Ellery.
Agent: Hello, Mr. Ellery. Could you confirm your billing zip code and the last four digits of your card for verification?
Customer: Sure, the zip code is 80204 and the last four are 4192.
Agent: Thank you. How can I help you today?
Customer: Well, I have a charge from BrightBench Assembly Co that I need to talk to someone about. It was for $340.00.
Agent: All right, let me pull up your account. Do you happen to have the date of the charge or the statement it was on?
Customer: It was charged around early August, and it shows up on my statement date of August 19, 2026.
Agent: I see the $340.00 charge from BrightBench Assembly Co on August 9th. Can you explain what happened with this purchase?
Customer: Yeah, I paid them in advance to come over and assemble some big furniture pieces I bought. But the technician never showed up.
Agent: Did they ever follow up with you or attempt to reschedule the appointment?
Customer: No, nobody called, nobody texted, nothing. They just didn't come, and they never rescheduled.
Agent: Have you tried reaching out to BrightBench Assembly Co directly since the missed appointment?
Customer: I did try calling their main number twice, but it just went to an automated voicemail, and I never got a call back.
Agent: Okay, and when did you try reaching out to them?
Customer: Honestly, I put off calling for weeks because work was completely crazy, so I only called them about a week or two ago, and now I'm checking with you guys.
Agent: I understand. So to make sure I have the full picture, you paid $340.00 upfront to BrightBench Assembly Co for furniture assembly, the technician never showed up, they didn't reach out to reschedule, and your calls to them haven't been returned.
Customer: Yes, that's exactly what happened.
